clue.text: A church covered with faux antique carpet

parts.note: a repro is a reproduction, a fake antique
taken as written
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church floor hidden under a fake antique rug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'covered with' means the first part sits on top, so it comes first; a repro is a reproduction piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is an informal British verb for giving them a dressing-down, a scolding or reproof.

clue.text: Time to leave pop star to warble

indicators.note: the named letter goes away, so it is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: Sting is the former Police frontman
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pop singer is told it is time to go and sing elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: STING without its T leaves SING.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to sing with trills, so both verbs describe producing a tune with the voice.

clue.text: Chicken suffering from flatulence

definitions.meaning: second meaning: troubled by wind in the gut

explanation.surface: A poultry bird with digestive gas trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' reads as the bird, but it is the slang adjective for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is informal British slang for nervous or cowardly, and literally describes someone with intestinal gas.

clue.text: Precise answer to conservative clergyman

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman with conservative views gives an exact reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and precise are synonyms, both meaning exactly correct without error.

clue.text: Saw nothing wrong in US state

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so these letters must be put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness in America claims to have seen nothing amiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington is a state in the Pacific Northwest of the USA.

clue.text: Cell in which you are in element

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the preceding letters go within the element

parts.note: neon is a chemical element, a noble gas
text-speak: U for you, R for are

explanation.surface: A cell in which you feel completely at home, in your element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In your element' is the idiom the surface plays on; here the element is a chemical one, with U R placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic cell of the nervous system.

clue.text: Iron Lady in retirement pursuing scaled down campaign for women's rights

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so one piece is placed after another

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
mini means small-scale

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, in retirement following a small women's rights campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' looks like one unit, Thatcher's nickname, but splits into iron (FE) and a lady's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminism is the movement advocating equal rights and opportunities for women.

clue.text: Cell for American of no fixed address

definitions.note: what Americans call a cell, the British call this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British word for the portable phone Americans call a cell
second meaning: moving about, not settled in one place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell for American' sounds like a prison for a US citizen; it means the British equivalent of an American cellphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile is a portable phone in British English, and mobile as an adjective means able to move about freely.

clue.text: Gently persuaded female student to accept a kiss

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the student holds the other letters inside

parts.note: coed is US slang for a female student at a mixed college
A as written; X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A young woman at college was gently talked into accepting a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade someone by gentle flattery or patience, so coaxed is its past tense.

clue.text: Doctor heartlessly unprescribing medicine

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: without its heart the word loses everything in the middle, leaving only its two ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the word survive

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted doctor refuses to prescribe medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unprescribing' is not a real word; it is chosen for its first letter U and last letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug is a medicine or any substance used to treat illness.

clue.text: Excesses of posh girl stirring up a hue and cry

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is a mass noun for such behaviour

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, an upper-class young woman entering society

indicators.note: stirring something up mixes it around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of a, hue and cry; 'and' only joins them

explanation.surface: A well-bred young woman behaving wildly and causing a public outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: A hue and cry is a public clamour; here 'and' is just glue and the other letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Debauchery is indulgence in sensual pleasures to excess, so it names excessive dissolute behaviour.

clue.text: Fruit which could give person energy

parts.note: a man is a person
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit that might give someone an energy boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Sandy has to take the biscuit!

parts.note: sandy and ginger both describe reddish hair
the 's of 'Ginger's', short for has
nap is an old slang verb meaning to seize or steal

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a red-haired person really takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being outrageous; here Sandy is a hair colour, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp biscuit flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: King's boring tendency to show knowledge

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex); the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A monarch's dull habit of showing off what he knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge gained through study, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: Reportedly deal with composer

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to handle something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Apparently someone must deal with a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal with' as a phrase gives the verb; 'with' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: Brief demise by way of bullet oddly to be desired

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: an end is a death or demise
via means by way of

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions are the ones kept, skipping every second letter

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A quick death by bullet, strangely, is something to wish for.
explanation.definitionFit: Enviable describes something others would want, so it is worth desiring.

clue.text: Queer Street for me

indicators.note: queer here means odd or strange, so the letters are set out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being in Queer Street, an old British phrase for being in debt, is the fate the speaker foresees.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is a British idiom for financial trouble; the setter of a crossword commonly refers to themself as 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords 'me' or 'I' often stands for the setter, the person who compiled the puzzle.

clue.text: Rudolf, for example, lifting thinner partner in embrace

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting raises the word so it reads from bottom to top
an embrace wraps around someone, so the partner is held inside the other word

parts.note: reedier means more reed-like: thinner and higher in tone
North partners South in bridge, so N can be a partner

explanation.surface: Rudolph the reindeer raising a slimmer partner in a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partners are named by compass points, so a single N or S can stand for partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf the red-nosed reindeer is the most famous of Santa's sleigh-pullers, an example of the animal.

clue.text: Five bared bust shamelessly, perhaps

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Five people baring their chests with no shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a chest but signals the mix; 'shamelessly' is an example of the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamelessly modifies a verb and ends in -ly, so it is an example of an adverb.

clue.text: Watched terribly verbose daughter

indicators.note: doing something terribly means doing it badly, so the letters fall into a muddle

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent kept an eye on a very long-winded daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully, so observed is the past tense for watched.

clue.text: Pub employees exclude males

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
men are males

explanation.surface: A pub's staff refuse to let men in.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmen are men who serve drinks behind a bar, so they are pub workers.

clue.text: It's found in forge in Indian village

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Something you would find in a smithy in a village in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like the indicator, but it belongs to the definition; the second 'in' points to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block on which a blacksmith hammers metal in a forge.

clue.text: Imprisoned old Peruvian

wordplay.note: can is US slang for a jail, so a prisoner is in it; read the two words run together

explanation.surface: An ancient inhabitant of Peru who was locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: In US slang, the can is a jail, so someone imprisoned is 'in can' when the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire in Peru until the Spanish conquest, so an Incan is an old Peruvian.

clue.text: Stew of scarce tuna and lobster?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seafood stew made with scarce tuna and lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows that a lobster is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large marine crustacean with a hard shell and claws.

clue.text: Children heading away from slides

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and it goes away here

parts.note: skids are slides on a slippery surface

explanation.surface: Children rushing off from the playground slides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides' looks like playground equipment but means skids.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids is the informal word for children.

clue.text: Quick look round part of castle

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick glance

explanation.surface: A quick look around a section of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest central tower of a castle.

clue.text: About to pursue sale of goods to the consumer

definitions.text: sale of goods to the consumer

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the selling of goods directly to the public, as opposed to wholesale.

clue.text: Couple get grant to make piece of jewellery

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A couple receive a grant so they can make jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn around the wrist, a type of jewellery.
